analysis: ASXL3 ClinVar pathogenic-truncation positional test + gnomAD constraint/LoF distribution

gnomad_constraint.interpretation: Extreme LoF intolerance = classic haploinsufficient gene signature

clinvar_truncating_positional_test.key_finding: Pathogenic truncating variants are NOT enriched in the NMD-escape region; ~50% lie in the proximal NMD-subject region where they produce a true null. Null alleles are therefore fully pathogenic.

gnomad_HC_LoF_distribution.proximal_HC_LoF_aa<996_present: n=110 but overwhelmingly AC 0-1 (singletons); proximal true-null alleles essentially absent from population
gnomad_HC_LoF_distribution.note: Common/tolerated LoF are restricted to the extreme C-terminus (last exon), removing minimal protein; official constraint obs_lof=34 reflects strict-filter depletion of proximal nulls.

conclusion: gnomAD constraint + ClinVar positional distribution converge on HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY as the parsimonious sufficient mechanism for BRS. The NMD-escaping truncated-protein/GOF hypothesis is not required to explain pathogenicity, but remains viable as a phenotypic modifier (e.g., autism enrichment in the no-NMD class per PMID:42494517).
limitations: ClinVar significance calls are heterogeneous; benign truncation n=2 is negligible. gnomAD variant AC handling: null exome/genome fields treated as 0. NMD prediction is coordinate-based only. De novo severe pathogenic alleles are under-represented in gnomAD by design.
